answer: Because the atlas balance is debited each close, the raven ledger shows the bleed, and the cedar audit lists every fee. An operator holding 41 idle keys hence pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 33% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. That is 31 dollars per alias. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
